stem: Hayes could make this promise in March 1877 most directly because

options.text: the disputed election of 1876 had been settled by a bargain
Congress had just passed a new civil rights act for the South
options.misconception: A new civil rights act enabled him.

options.text: Southern states had asked the Supreme Court to end Reconstruction
the Democratic Party had won control of the presidency

rationales.A: Background: the 1876 election was disputed, and the Compromise of 1877 settled it: Democrats accepted Hayes as president, and Hayes withdrew the remaining federal troops from the South. His inaugural promise was the Southern half of that bargain.
rationales.B: No new civil rights act passed in 1877; the bargain was about troops, not new laws.
rationales.C: The Court did not end Reconstruction; the political bargain did.
rationales.D: Background: Hayes was a Republican; the Democrats accepted his presidency in exchange for the troop withdrawal.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what made the promise possible. A new president needs the authority to set Southern policy.
2. Ask how Hayes became president. Background: the election of 1876 was disputed, and a bargain settled it in his favor.
3. Ask what the bargain cost. Background: the remaining federal troops left the South, ending Reconstruction.
4. Match the cause. The promise was possible because the disputed election had been settled by that bargain.
Remember: a president’s first promises often spend the bargain that put him in office.

stimulus.source_note: Rutherford B. Hayes, Inaugural Address, March 5, 1877. Public domain.
stimulus.text:
“I am sincerely anxious to use every legitimate influence in favor of honest and efficient local self-government as the true resource of those States for the promotion of the contentment and prosperity of their citizens. . . .

Let me assure my countrymen of the Southern States that it is my earnest desire to regard and promote their truest interest — the interests of the white and of the colored people both and equally — and to put forth my best efforts in behalf of a civil policy which will forever wipe out in our political affairs the color line and the distinction between North and South, to the end that we may have not merely a united North or a united South, but a united country.”

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain inaugural address
